headers.comment: Vite fingerprints these filenames, so a given URL's contents never change. Cache them hard.

The entry document points at the fingerprinted bundles, so it must never be cached. Both paths are listed because Hosting matches these globs against the path the BROWSER asked for, before resolving anything: a visitor requests "/", and the rewrite to /index.html happens afterwards. Matching only "/index.html" silently did nothing, so the default max-age=3600 applied and deploys appeared not to land for up to an hour. These three rules do not overlap, so which one wins never has to be reasoned about.

firestore.comment: Without this, the CLI has no idea where the rules live and `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` fails with 'no targets match'. The rules are the actual security boundary, so they belong in version control and in a deploy command — not pasted into the console by hand, where the repo copy and the live copy silently drift apart.

functions.comment: Two predeploy steps. install, because the CLI analyses this source locally to work out what to deploy and cannot resolve firebase-functions without node_modules present — a fresh clone would otherwise fail with 'Couldn't find firebase-functions package'. Then copy-seed stages src/data into functions/seed, because `firebase deploy` only uploads this directory; the staged copy is gitignored and regenerated every time, so it cannot drift from the app.
